Split at the conversation level before deriving examples, augmentations, or tokenization statistics. Every message from a conversation must remain in one partition; also check repeated or forwarded messages across conversations. If deployment predicts future conversations, use a chronological group split and document any user-level overlap. Fit preprocessing and choose hyperparameters using training and validation only; retain an untouched test set.

Audit token lengths and the actual retained text against labels. Assumption: the final sentence is available when production inference runs. Under that assumption, compare tail-preserving truncation, a larger supported token budget, and windowed encoding with conversation-level aggregation. Select using validation results and latency constraints. If the final sentence is unavailable at prediction time, remove it consistently and redefine the task rather than importing future information.

Mean pooling must multiply token representations by the attention mask and divide by the count of retained tokens, excluding padding; explicitly decide whether special tokens contribute. Reject or handle examples with no contributing tokens instead of dividing by zero.

Re-evaluate the corrected pipeline with per-class precision, recall, macro-F1, confusion matrices, and length-stratified results. Report truncation frequency and conversation-level uncertainty. Expect scores to fall when leakage disappears; use the corrected split for subsequent decisions.
answers.verification: Propose assertions that conversation IDs are disjoint, duplicated content is audited, padding changes do not change pooled representations, and long-example retention follows the chosen policy. Review representative tokenized examples and evaluate once on the held-out test partition.

The implementation validates both container shapes and every value before computing the result, with invalid inputs reported as ValueError. Labels must be integer indices and explicitly exclude bool. Logits are unnormalized scores; applying softmax before this function would change the objective and its derivative. Assumption: numeric logits use Python's built-in int or float representations; boolean logits retain Python's numeric interpretation, because only boolean labels are explicitly prohibited by the supplied contract.

Subtracting the largest logit before exponentiation prevents exponential overflow. Cross-entropy uses the log-sum-exp expression directly, avoiding log of a probability that underflows to zero. The batch objective is the mean, so every gradient row is divided by the number of examples, not the number of classes. Normalizing loss contributions before summing also avoids unnecessary overflow from a large batch sum. Extremely separated finite scores can still have a mathematically valid loss beyond float range.

For proposed finite-difference verification, perturb each score of a small moderate-valued matrix by plus and minus epsilon, estimate the central difference of the returned loss, and compare with the corresponding analytic gradient using absolute and relative tolerances. Also check invariance to adding a constant to each row and zero row sums in the gradient. These checks have not been executed.
answers.verification: Propose finite differences on moderate logits, uniform-logit loss log(class_count), confidently wrong predictions, row-shift invariance, gradient row sums, and invalid shapes/types/indices including boolean labels and nonfinite logits. Do not execute the implementation.

Keep request tracing focused on user work. Exclude successful routine health probes from tracing at the instrumentation boundary, while retaining probe counts and availability signals separately. Decide explicitly whether failed probes produce diagnostic spans or bounded logs so outages remain observable. Configure one tracer provider and exporter pipeline, avoiding duplicate automatic and manual spans.

At queue publication, inject the configured OpenTelemetry propagation fields into message metadata. At consumption, extract that metadata and start the processing span with the extracted remote context; attach and detach context per delivery using a finally block. Never rely on ambient context carried between workers. Missing or malformed context starts an independent trace. For batches or fan-in, use span links where a single parent would misrepresent causality; record retries and outcomes with bounded attributes.

Add duration histograms and request/error counters with route templates, service, and status classes. Define p95 windows and failure ratios with minimum traffic, sustained thresholds, and an SLO burn-rate policy. Page for material ongoing user impact; reserve individual slow traces for investigation. Sampling must not determine metric denominators.

Remove customer text from logs at source. Allowlist operational fields, sanitize exception content, and keep identifiers bounded and non-sensitive. Document retention and access controls. Correlate safe logs with trace/span IDs instead of copying payloads.
answers.verification: Propose end-to-end producer/consumer correlation checks, concurrent delivery isolation, malformed-carrier and redelivery cases, and exporter-failure behavior. Inspect telemetry for customer text and cardinality growth. Exercise alert windows with sustained failures, isolated slow requests, and low traffic; verify metric coverage despite trace sampling.

For the supplied five samples, baseline median is 8 ms and candidate median is 5 ms: a 37.5% median reduction. Baseline mean is (32 + 80) / 5 = 22.4 ms; candidate mean is (20 + 120) / 5 = 28 ms, a 25% increase. Nearest-rank p95 selects rank ceil(0.95 × 5) = 5, so baseline p95 is 80 ms and candidate p95 is 120 ms, a 50% increase. These are descriptive sample statistics; five observations provide weak evidence about production tails.

The candidate therefore improves the typical observed request while worsening both supplied mean and tail observations. It has not met an objective that includes tail latency and memory. Excluding timeouts and cold starts biases the reported comparison. Restore their counts and outcomes, state timeout thresholds, and distinguish completed-request latency from timeout probability; a timed-out request's true completion latency is censored.

Collect comparable cold and warm workloads, realistic key distributions, hit rates, concurrency, request sizes, and cache invalidation behavior. Measure peak and steady memory, allocation pressure, eviction costs, and saturation alongside latency and throughput. Specify tail and memory acceptance limits before rerunning. Keep the baseline available if those limits fail; the supplied median improvement alone does not justify adoption.
answers.verification: Propose repeated interleaved baseline/candidate runs on equivalent hardware and datasets, with warmup and cold-start policies stated. Retain raw observations and all failures, collect enough samples for tail uncertainty, and compare confidence intervals plus memory budgets. No benchmark has been executed.

Resolve an explicitly supplied relative path against the invocation directory and report its resolved location on failure. Locate bundled defaults using importlib.resources, not the current directory or assumptions about a source checkout. Keep writable user configuration outside the installed package. Assumption: no existing published configuration-location contract must be preserved; otherwise retain it through a documented compatibility path.

Declare the actual runtime dependency in project metadata with justified version constraints; place test and build dependencies in their appropriate groups. Remove reliance on the maintainer's environment. Define the console command in [project.scripts] pointing to an included importable main function, and ensure package discovery and resource inclusion put that module and defaults into both wheel and sdist.

State requires-python consistently with support for 3.11 through 3.14, and audit source syntax and dependencies against that range. Build artifacts in an isolated environment, inspect their contents and metadata, then install the wheel into fresh environments for each supported minor version. The callback has two independent lifetime defects: Vec pushes can invalidate its data pointer, and the foreign registration can outlive its Rust owner. Concurrent callbacks also create data races unless every shared access follows a synchronization protocol. Reserving capacity merely delays reallocation and does not solve lifetime or concurrency.

Assumption: the C API accepts a user-data pointer and provides unregister semantics that can be documented. Put callback context in stable heap storage, such as a Box containing synchronized state, and pass its allocation address rather than a pointer into movable Vec elements. A Box<Vec<T>> stabilizes the Vec header, not its element buffer. Use a boxed slice for fixed element storage or redesign the callback to access the Vec through the context under a lock; never retain element references across a mutation or unlock.

Keep the context alive until unregister prevents new callbacks and all in-flight callbacks finish. Serialize shutdown and callback admission, release locks before waiting, and reclaim the allocation exactly once. If unregister does not provide quiescence, add the API-supported completion barrier or retain storage until safety can be guaranteed; a stop flag alone is insufficient.

Document pointer validity, thread permissions, lock ordering, and callback reentrancy. Prevent Rust panics from crossing the C ABI and define a safe error outcome. If these guarantees are unavailable, the wrapper cannot offer safe ownership.
answers.verification: Propose a controllable C test shim that forces reallocations, concurrent callbacks, reentrancy, and callbacks paused during shutdown. Check unregister/quiescence ordering and exactly-once reclamation. Use appropriate sanitizer builds and Rust-side model/lifetime checks where supported; none alone proves foreign API guarantees.

The artifact defines a callable contract checker without invoking it or performing import-time work. It checks both boundaries and several interior values, including an integer too large for an accidental fixed-width conversion. The result must be an integer equal to the input; asserting only equality would allow an implementation returning float or bool to slip through. Assumption: 'returned unchanged' describes the integer value and type, not object identity, so the checker does not impose an identity requirement.

Wrong-type cases cover booleans explicitly, numeric-looking strings, integral and fractional floats, null, bytes, and common containers. These must raise TypeError even when their apparent numeric content is within range. Integer cases below and above the allowed interval must raise ValueError, including large magnitudes. This separates type validation from range validation and catches implementations that coerce input, clamp values, or use the wrong boundary comparison.

The exception helper fails if the call returns normally or raises the wrong exception family. Other exceptions escape as failures rather than being swallowed. The checker does not inspect implementation details, mutate arguments, or depend on testing frameworks. Its intended use is check_contract(normalize_port) in the evaluator's own harness; no execution or pass result is claimed here.
answers.verification: Propose running this checker against the supplied implementation and deliberate mutants: accepting bool, converting strings/floats, using exclusive endpoints, clamping invalid integers, returning a float, and raising one exception type for every error. The artifact has not been executed.

Choose one PostgreSQL transaction for claim, job, outbox event, and stored replay response. Authenticate the tenant first. Scope a non-null idempotency key by tenant and endpoint, enforce that unique constraint, and store a canonical semantic request fingerprint. Assumption: retries reuse their key; distinct keys may intentionally submit identical work. Define the retention window explicitly so clients know when replay protection expires.

Within the transaction, attempt INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for the claim. With READ COMMITTED, an overlapping insert waits for the first transaction's resolution. If it commits, a subsequent statement reads its completed claim; matching payload returns the saved status/body, while a changed payload returns 409 without another job. If it rolls back, the waiting request can acquire the claim. Bound lock waits and return a retryable response on timeout; never steal a pending transaction's key.

The winner creates one job and its outbox row, saves the response and job ID in the claim, then commits. Any crash before commit rolls everything back. A lost reply after commit is recovered by replay. No claim is separately committed, so abandoned-claim leases are unnecessary.

Dispatch the outbox asynchronously with retries. Delivery may repeat if a dispatcher crashes after sending; consumers must deduplicate by event/job identity. This prevents duplicate submission records without promising exactly-once external side effects.
answers.verification: Propose overlapping same-key requests, cross-tenant keys, payload mismatch, blocked-transaction timeout, rollback before commit, and lost-reply-after-commit cases. Verify one committed job/outbox pair and identical replay responses. Simulate dispatcher resend and consumer deduplication; no execution is proposed against production.
